long_distance_conduits.name: Long-Distance Conduits
long_distance_conduits.observation: The new conduit taps springs two days' walk away, tunnels through two ridges and crosses the valley on a double tier of arches.
long_distance_conduits.social_consequence: The city drinks hill water in every season, and it now depends on a single channel that an enemy or an earthquake can cut.

reused_stone_building.name: Stone Reuse
reused_stone_building.observation: The old hall's columns and dressed blocks are carted off to build the new walls, and the ruins shrink year by year.

reservoir_valve_pits.name: Reservoir Valve Pits
reservoir_valve_pits.observation: A stone-lined pit at the foot of the dam holds a bronze valve, and the keeper opens it by measure in the dry months.

open_town_cisterns.name: Open Town Cisterns
open_town_cisterns.observation: A walled basin the size of a field holds enough water inside the town to outlast a summer siege.

great_tank_reservoirs.name: Great Tanks
great_tank_reservoirs.observation: An earthen bank a mile long holds back the rainy-season run-off, and channels carry it to fields three villages away.
great_tank_reservoirs.social_consequence: Whole districts farm by the tank's water, and the tank's keepers and their dues become the most powerful people in the country.

lead_sheet_roofing.name: Lead Roofing
lead_sheet_roofing.observation: Sheets of cast lead are laid over the dome's timbers, lapped and rolled at the seams, and shed the rain for a century.

thin_brick_shell_vaults.name: Thin Brick Vaults
thin_brick_shell_vaults.observation: Flat bricks laid in quick-setting mortar climb in leaning courses until the vault closes, without a stick of centring.

pendentive_domes.name: Pendentive Domes
pendentive_domes.observation: Four curved triangles of brick rise from the corners of the square bay and meet in a ring, and the dome sits on the ring as if floating.
pendentive_domes.ability_reason: Curved triangles of masonry let a round dome sit on a square bay, so great halls can be roofed in masonry over open floors.
pendentive_domes.social_consequence: The great domed hall becomes the ruler's proudest work, and years of levies and hauling are spent to raise it.

buttressing_half_domes.name: Half-Dome Buttressing
buttressing_half_domes.observation: Two half-domes lean against the great dome from east and west, catching its thrust and carrying it down to the ground.

stepwells.name: Stepwells
stepwells.observation: Flights of stone stairs descend seven storeys to the water, and the shaded landings stay cool even in the dry season.

open_spandrel_arch_bridges.name: Open-Spandrel Bridges
open_spandrel_arch_bridges.observation: One long, flat arch leaps the river, and small arches pierced through its shoulders let the floodwater pass instead of pushing it over.
open_spandrel_arch_bridges.ability_reason: A flat segmental arch with openings in its shoulders spans a wide river with less stone and lets floodwater pass through.

bracket_set_timber_towers.name: Bracket-Set Towers
bracket_set_timber_towers.observation: Clusters of interlocking wooden brackets carry each eave of the tower, and they flex together when the earth shakes.

plank_walled_timber_halls.name: Plank-Walled Halls
plank_walled_timber_halls.observation: Great posts sunk in the ground carry the roof, and split planks set upright between them wall in the chief's long hall.

horseshoe_arches.name: Horseshoe Arches
horseshoe_arches.observation: The arch swells wider than its opening before closing at the top, resting on columns carried from older buildings.

domed_steam_baths.name: Steam Baths
domed_steam_baths.observation: Light falls through star-shaped holes in the dome onto bathers sweating on hot marble, while a furnace below heats the floor.

channelled_garden_courts.name: Channelled Gardens
channelled_garden_courts.observation: Narrow stone channels cross the court, and water from the fountain where they meet runs out to every flower bed.

river_diversion_weirs.name: Diversion Weirs
river_diversion_weirs.observation: A low weir of stone and brushwood across the river lifts the water just enough to spill it into the canal mouth.

carved_stucco.name: Carved Stucco
carved_stucco.observation: Wet plaster over the brick is carved into vines and lettering before it sets, and the hall looks as if hung with lace.

cross_domed_halls.name: Cross-Domed Halls
cross_domed_halls.observation: Four barrel vaults meet under a central dome on four piers, and the plan of the hall is a cross within a square.

pointed_arches.name: Pointed Arches
pointed_arches.observation: The mason sets two curves of stone leaning together, and the arch stands higher and presses less on its walls.
pointed_arches.ability_reason: Two arcs meeting at a point push down more steeply than a round arch, so walls can be thinner and openings taller.

corbelled_spire_towers.name: Corbelled Spires
corbelled_spire_towers.observation: Each course of stone juts a little inward over the one below, until the tower closes in a tall curved peak.

wind_catchers.name: Wind Catchers
wind_catchers.observation: A tower on the roof with openings toward the wind draws the breeze down into the rooms and across a pool of water.

marsh_causeways.name: Marsh Causeways
marsh_causeways.observation: Timber piles driven into the bog carry a paved road, and carts cross the marsh where men once waded to the waist.

intersecting_rib_domes.name: Ribbed Domes
intersecting_rib_domes.observation: Arches cross each other under the dome in a star, and the thin shell between them rests on their ribs.

brick_stair_towers.name: Brick Stair Towers
brick_stair_towers.observation: A stair inside the tall brick tower winds up to a gallery, where a crier can be heard across the whole town.

mill_leats.name: Mill Leats
mill_leats.observation: A dam across the stream feeds a dug channel to the wheel, and a tail-race returns the water to the stream below the mill.

cutwater_pier_bridges.name: Cutwater Bridges
cutwater_pier_bridges.observation: Pointed stone piers split the current and the ice floes, and the timber deck between them is renewed every few decades.

canal_locks.observation: The lock keeper shuts the lower gates and opens the sluice above, and the barge rises slowly in its stone chamber to the next reach.
canal_locks.ability_reason: A chamber with gates at both ends lifts boats between water levels without the rush of a flash lock, so canals can climb hills.
canal_locks.social_consequence: Barges carry grain and stone far inland, and the canal needs keepers, dredgers and toll-takers year after year.

estuary_embankments.name: Estuary Embankments
estuary_embankments.observation: A bank of clay and turf holds back the spring tides, and the salt marsh behind it becomes sheep pasture and then plough land.
estuary_embankments.social_consequence: New land is won from the sea, and the villages behind the bank now live or drown by its upkeep.

newel_spiral_stairs.name: Newel Stairs
newel_spiral_stairs.observation: Each stone step carries its own slice of the central post, and the stair winds up the tower in a space no wider than a man's arms.

percussion_drilled_wells.name: Percussion-Drilled Wells
percussion_drilled_wells.observation: A heavy iron bit on a cane cable is lifted and dropped for months, and the brine rises from hundreds of feet below.

crib_work_quays.name: Crib-Work Quays
crib_work_quays.observation: Log boxes sunk along the waterline and filled with stones make a quay where ships can tie up and unload directly.

honeycomb_corbel_vaults.name: Honeycomb Vaults
honeycomb_corbel_vaults.observation: Tiers of small niches, each corbelled out over the last, fill the corners of the vault like the cells of a comb.

four_hall_courtyards.name: Four-Hall Courtyards
four_hall_courtyards.observation: On each side of the court a great vaulted hall opens to the air, for teaching, for prayer and for shade.

masonry_buttressing.observation: Piers of stone built out from the wall where each vault presses against it keep the wall from leaning outward.

vaulted_cloister_walks.name: Vaulted Cloisters
vaulted_cloister_walks.observation: A covered walk round the garden lets the brothers read and work in the dry, even in the long rains.

double_shell_domes.name: Double-Shell Domes
double_shell_domes.observation: A tall outer dome rises over a low inner one, so the dome looks grand from the city and well proportioned from within.

rib_vaults.name: Rib Vaults
rib_vaults.observation: The masons build the stone ribs first on light centring, then fill the panels between them with thin stone that needs no support of its own.
rib_vaults.ability_reason: Stone ribs built first on light centring carry thin infill panels, so vaults can span wider and odder-shaped bays with less stone and less timber.

self_closing_tide_gates.name: Self-Closing Tide Gates
self_closing_tide_gates.observation: Hinged doors in the sluice swing open to drain the fields at low tide and are pushed shut by the rising sea.

glazed_tile_domes.name: Tile-Faced Domes
glazed_tile_domes.observation: Blue and turquoise tiles cover the dome, shedding the rain and flashing in the sun a day's ride away.

latrine_chute_towers.name: Latrine Towers
latrine_chute_towers.observation: Privies in a tower at the end of the dormitory drop into a chute over the stream, well away from the well and the kitchens.

roof_treadwheel_cranes.name: Roof Treadwheel Cranes
roof_treadwheel_cranes.observation: Two men walking inside a great wheel in the roof space raise the vault stones up through a hole in the floor.

putlog_scaffolding.name: Putlog Scaffolding
putlog_scaffolding.observation: Poles slotted into square holes left in the wall carry the scaffold, and the holes are filled when the work comes down.

piped_town_conduits.name: Piped Town Conduits
piped_town_conduits.observation: Lead pipes carry spring water from the hill to a fountain in the market, where anyone may fill a bucket for free.

clustered_piers.name: Clustered Piers
clustered_piers.observation: Slender shafts bundled round each pier rise straight into the ribs of the vault, and the arcade stands taller than any before.

vaulted_undercrofts.name: Vaulted Undercrofts
vaulted_undercrofts.observation: Under the merchant's hall a stone-vaulted cellar keeps wine and wool cool, dry and safe from fire.

wall_chimneys.name: Wall Chimneys
wall_chimneys.observation: A hooded fireplace in the wall draws the smoke up a flue, and for the first time the upper room is warm and the rafters are not black with soot.
wall_chimneys.ability_reason: A fireplace in the wall with a flue to the roof takes the smoke out of the room, so houses can have upper floors, private rooms and clean air.
wall_chimneys.social_consequence: Families move off the open hearth into separate warm rooms, and the great hall where everyone slept together begins to empty.

flying_buttresses.name: Flying Buttresses
flying_buttresses.observation: Half-arches leap from the outer piers over the aisle roofs and press against the high wall just where the vault pushes out.
flying_buttresses.ability_reason: Arches leaping over the aisles carry the vault's thrust to outer piers, freeing the walls for tall windows.
flying_buttresses.social_consequence: The great temples rise higher than any building before them, and a town may spend three generations of wealth and labor finishing one.

bored_log_mains.name: Bored-Log Mains
bored_log_mains.observation: Elm logs bored end to end and tapered to fit are laid under the streets, carrying water to houses and cisterns.

buttress_pinnacles.name: Buttress Pinnacles
buttress_pinnacles.observation: A heavy stone pinnacle on top of each buttress presses down on it, turning the vault's push into a steadier load.

inhabited_bridges.name: Inhabited Bridges
inhabited_bridges.observation: Shops and houses crowd both sides of the stone bridge, and their rents pay for its repair.
inhabited_bridges.social_consequence: The bridge pays for itself, and when fire or flood takes it, a whole street of families goes into the river with it.

roof_flashing_interfaces.observation: Strips of lead are dressed into the joints where the roof meets the chimney and the wall, and the rain no longer creeps inside.

moulded_brick_architecture.name: Moulded Brick
moulded_brick_architecture.observation: Bricks pressed in carved moulds make tracery and cornices without a stone carver, and glazed ones gleam green and black in the wall.

masonry_repointing.observation: The masons rake the crumbling mortar out of the old joints and press in new, and the wall stands another century.

crown_post_roofs.name: Crown-Post Roofs
crown_post_roofs.observation: A post rising from each tie-beam carries a long plate under the collars, and braces keep the whole roof from racking.

carved_rain_spouts.name: Rain Spouts
carved_rain_spouts.observation: Carved beasts on the gutters spit rainwater far out from the walls, so it no longer soaks the foundations.

mortar_compatibility_assessment.observation: The master tests the old mortar's colour and softness before mixing the new, so the repair gives way before the stone does.

lead_rain_gutters.name: Lead Gutters
lead_rain_gutters.observation: Lead gutters along the eaves feed downpipes to the drains, and the lane below stays dry in a storm.

bar_tracery_windows.name: Bar Tracery
bar_tracery_windows.observation: Slender stone bars cut to the template branch into circles and trefoils, and the glaziers fill every opening with glass.
bar_tracery_windows.ability_reason: Thin stone bars cut from templates divide great windows into glazed lights, letting in far more daylight while the wall stays strong.

tracing_floor_templates.name: Tracing Floors
tracing_floor_templates.observation: The master scratches the full-size window into the plaster floor, and the carpenters cut wooden templates from his lines.

stone_merchant_houses.name: Stone Merchant Houses
stone_merchant_houses.observation: The merchant lives above a vaulted stone shop with a door on the street, and his goods are safe when the timber houses burn.

rose_windows.name: Rose Windows
rose_windows.observation: Tracery spokes radiate from the centre like the petals of a flower, and the great round window glows over the west door.

covered_cloth_halls.name: Cloth Halls
covered_cloth_halls.observation: The cloth hall is a long covered building where every bolt is laid out, measured and sealed before it is sold.

jettied_timber_houses.name: Jettied Houses
jettied_timber_houses.observation: Each upper floor juts out over the one below, and the lane beneath is dark, crowded and easily set alight.
jettied_timber_houses.social_consequence: More families fit inside the walls, and a spark in one kitchen can burn down a whole street.

belfry_town_halls.name: Belfry Town Halls
belfry_town_halls.observation: The council meets above the market hall under a tall belfry, and the charters sit in an iron chest in the tower strongroom.
belfry_town_halls.ability_reason: A town hall with a bell tower gives the council a seat, a strongroom for its charters and a bell to call citizens to arms or to assembly.
belfry_town_halls.social_consequence: The town's council has a building as proud as the ruler's hall, and its bell, not the lord's, now marks the town's days.

stone_party_walls.name: Stone Party Walls
stone_party_walls.observation: By ordinance every new house must share a stone wall with its neighbour, so a fire stops at the wall instead of taking the street.

tiled_stoves.name: Tiled Stoves
tiled_stoves.observation: A great stove of glazed tiles in the corner of the room stores the heat of a small fire and gives it back all night, without smoke.

toll_paved_streets.name: Paved Streets
toll_paved_streets.observation: Tolls on carts at the gates pay for cobbles, and the main streets no longer turn to mud and dung in the rain.

geometric_design_rules.name: Geometric Design Rules
geometric_design_rules.observation: The master sets out each pier with compass and square from the width of the hall, and the proportions hold as the building rises.

house_glass_windows.name: Glazed House Windows
house_glass_windows.observation: Small diamond panes set in lead let light into the merchant's parlour while keeping out the wind and rain.

arcaded_market_squares.name: Arcaded Squares
arcaded_market_squares.observation: Arcades on all four sides of the square keep buyers and sellers dry, and the market goes on through the rain.

flat_segmental_bridges.name: Flat Segmental Bridges
flat_segmental_bridges.observation: Three wide, shallow arches span the river where five narrow ones stood before, and barges pass beneath with room to spare.
